utterances.text: Sir, later on in the course of events, did you ever discuss with your brother any problems that he had in the KP Dom in his position as temporary warden or didn't you do that?

utterances.speaker: ARSENIJE KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We never talked about KP Dom problems except when I would come back from a long trip and I would tell him how tired I was, and he would just shrug his shoulders and tell me to get a rest and then go on working.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: He never told you about any efforts he made to get out of the position as temporary warden; right?

utterances.speaker: ARSENIJE KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not to me. He didn't have time to. He was too busy trying to get hold of food and animal feed. He didn't have time to get a rest even.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Sir, throughout your testimony, you stressed that he was the temporary warden. However, in July 1992, the Ministry of Justice appointed him to be the permanent warden. You're aware of this, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: ARSENIJE KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally am not aware of that, and it was not my job to get to know such things. I addressed directors, jokingly, as commercial people. And he never talked to me about this, actually, and I never asked.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Sir, you said that you never heard that a detainee escaped. Did you ever hear that a guard or a member of the KP Dom administration was disciplined for not taking their duties properly? Are you aware of anything like this?

utterances.speaker: ARSENIJE KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that, because I wasn't around. I don't even know about things that happened before the war, and even less could I know about anybody being disciplined for violations or dodging his duties.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Sir, the KP Dom had a storage for benzine, right, gas, diesel; right?

utterances.speaker: ARSENIJE KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was a garage which had been vacated to make room and served for the storage of fuel, oil, and petrol.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And your brother, Milorad, filled the tank of the red Yugo, the second red Yugo, at this depot; right?

utterances.speaker: ARSENIJE KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not dispose of any fuel, and I don't know about that at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Sir, you told us earlier on that besides transporting goods, you also drove detainees to the farm. You remember that; right? You talked about that.

utterances.speaker: ARSENIJE KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Who gave you these assignments? Who ordered you to do that?

utterances.speaker: ARSENIJE KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The officer, the man on duty of the Dom.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you mean the guard on duty who was sitting in the entrance gate, or who?

utterances.speaker: ARSENIJE KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one who was on duty at the gate. He would call me to park my car outside the entrance and to take people to the farm.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And where did he find you? Where were you usually?

utterances.speaker: ARSENIJE KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would usually get together in a former office for drivers, from that place to the canteen, which was outside the compound, and that's where we had lunch and coffee.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The former office for the drivers, where was it? Was it within the administration building?

utterances.speaker: ARSENIJE KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was outside the administration building, in the compound, in the compound, and when you look at the gate, it was towards the entrance into the metalwork shop.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I would like to show the witness the huge plan, Exhibit 6, P6.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Sir, I hope you can see it. Are you able to see on the map where this is?

utterances.speaker: ARSENIJE KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who drew this? If someone tells me where the building is, then maybe I could show you. I'm not a construction engineer to be able to read this plan.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: ARSENIJE KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it were written in Serbian, then perhaps I would be able to find something here.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Sir, we'll put it on the ELMO and we'll try to make it bigger on your computer screen, because there is writing in Serbian on the map and you may be able to see it, with the help of the technical people.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We can't see it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm afraid we still have an image of the courtroom taken from your back, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: -- on the computer. You can put it down again. Thanks very much, usher. We've now got the ELMO back.
